# std.window

Sliding-window folds and stateful windows (round 7, `lib/sequence-patterns.md`).   `a.window_fold(k, op)` and `Window(op)` keep two stacks for every op today; the law-picked strategies of `lib/sequence-patterns.md` (a `Group` adds and subtracts, a `Selective` op keeps a monotone deque) wait on law-bound dispatch over op values. State that is not a fold implements `Track` (`push`/`pop`); two pointers, Mo and divide-and-conquer DP all accept a `Track`.

In prelude (no `use` needed): `Sweep`, `Undo`, `Undoing`, `Window`, `track`, `undoing`, `window_fold`.

## `struct Window<T, M: Op<T>>(op: M)`

A sliding fold queue over `op`.

Fields: `front: List<T>`.

- `fn new(op: M) -> Window<T, M>` — \(O(1)\); An empty window over `op`, kept as two stacks: the back folds as it grows, and the front holds suffix folds of the older elements.
- `fn push(mut self, x: T, at: ?Int = None)` — \(O(1)\) amortized calls of `op`; Push `x` at the back, as the newest element.; traps: when `at:` is given to a window that has unkeyed elements or the other way round, or
- `fn expire(mut self, before: Int)` — \(O(1)\) amortized calls of `op` per removed element; Remove every element pushed `at:` a place below `before`, oldest first.; traps: when the window has unkeyed elements
- `fn pop(mut self, x: T) where T: Eq` — \(O(1)\) amortized calls of `op`; Pop the front: remove the oldest element, `x`.; traps: on an empty window, or in a checked build when `x` is not the oldest element
- `@get fn all(self) -> ?T` — \(O(1)\); The fold of the current contents, oldest first (`op(op(x1, x2), x3)` for pushes `x1`, `x2`, `x3`), so a non-commutative op folds in push order; `None` when empty.
- `@get fn len(self) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The number of elements in the window: pushes minus pops.
- `@get fn is_empty(self) -> Bool` — \(O(1)\); Whether the window holds no elements.
- `@get fn items(self) -> yields T` — \(O(1)\) to make, \(O(1)\) per step; The elements in the window, oldest first.

## `struct Tracked<S, T>(pub state: S, add: (mut S, T) -> (), remove: (mut S, T) -> ())`

A `Track` built from a structure and two closures.

- `fn push(mut self, x: T)` — \(O(1)\) plus one call of `add`; Apply `x` at the back: one call of `add(state, x)`.; traps: never (beyond what `add` traps on)
- `fn pop(mut self, x: T)` — \(O(1)\) plus one call of `remove`; Take the front element `x` back out: one call of `remove(state, x)`.; traps: never (beyond what `remove` traps on)
- `@get fn state(self) -> S` — \(O(1)\); The structure with exactly the window's elements applied.

## `trait Undo`

A structure that can return to an earlier state, newest change first: `Dsu`, `ParityDsu`, `WeightedDsu`, `DsuWith`, `RollbackArray`, and any user struct with these two methods.

## `struct Undoing<S: Undo, T>(pub state: S, add: (mut S, T) -> ())`

The queue-undo trick: a `Track` over an `Undo` structure, so a window that adds at the back and drops from the front runs on a structure that can only undo its newest change (a rollback DSU in a two-pointer pass).

- `fn push(mut self, x: T)` — \(O(1)\) applications of `add` amortized; Push `x` at the back: one `add` on top of the current state.; traps: never (beyond what `add` traps on)
- `fn pop(mut self, x: T)` — \(O(\log n)\) applications of `add` amortized; Drop the front element, which must be `x`.; traps: on an empty `Undoing`
- `@get fn state(self) -> S` — \(O(1)\); The structure with exactly the window's elements applied.

## `struct Sweep<D: Domain, S: Track<D>>(pub state: S)`

A movable range over `D` feeding a `Track`, for Mo and divide-and-conquer DP.

- `fn new(state: S, start: ?Range<D> = None) -> Sweep<D, S>` — \(O(1)\), plus `start.len` pushes when `start` is given; A sweep over `state`, starting empty (or at `start`).; traps: never (beyond what `state.push` traps on)
- `fn move(mut self, to: Range<D>)` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{dl} \rvert + \lvert \mathit{dr} \rvert)\) pushes and pops, where `dl` and `dr` are the moves of the two ends; Slide to `to`, feeding `state` the positions that enter and leave.; traps: never (beyond what the state traps on)
- `@get fn range(self) -> Range<D>` — \(O(1)\); The current range: the positions whose pushes the state holds.

## Functions

- `fn window_fold<S: Indexed<D, T>, D: Domain, T: Eq, M: Op<T>>(self: S, k: 1.., op: M) -> yields T` — \(O(n)\) amortized calls of `op`; One fold of `op` per length-`k` window of `self`, left to right, kept the way `Window(op)` keeps it (two stacks).; traps: when `k < 1`
- `fn track<S, T>(state: S, add: (mut S, T) -> (), remove: (mut S, T) -> ()) -> Tracked<S, T>` — \(O(1)\); A `Track` over any structure: `add(mut state, x)` applies an element at the back and `remove(mut state, x)` takes the front one back out, so `ok` reads `w.state`.
- `fn undoing<S: Undo, T>(state: S, add: (mut S, T) -> ()) -> Undoing<S, T>` — \(O(1)\); `Undoing` over `state`, holding no elements; see there.

## Example

```cp
let xs = [2, 1, 3, 2, 4]
let w = xs.windows(3).map(v => v.sum()).collect()
print(w)
// output: 6 6 9
```
